title: Orientation-Derived Operational Regimes
purpose: Defines Orientation as the organizational classifier of RT operational regimes without privileging any specific regime family.

motivation.problem: RT operational regimes currently exist but lack a formally governed organizational basis for classification.
motivation.resolution: Orientation becomes the governing organizational structure from which operational regimes are classified.

core_definition.orientation_role: Orientation organizes lawful continuation under RT_core.
core_definition.classification_rule: An RT operational regime is classified by its orientation organization under declared admissibility, residue, and context conditions.
core_definition.trace_requirement: Every classified regime must constructively trace to RT_core.

governance_rules.name: Orientation Classification
governance_rules.statement: Orientation classifies operational regimes but is not itself an operational regime.

governance_rules.name: Orientation Organization
governance_rules.statement: Orientation organizes lawful continuation independently of residue stabilization.

governance_rules.name: Residue Separation
governance_rules.statement: Residue stabilizes continuation but does not classify operational regimes.

governance_rules.name: Time Separation
governance_rules.statement: Operational regime classification shall not depend upon temporal interpretation.

effects: Provides a universal classifier for future regime families.
Avoids introducing linearity as a privileged primitive.

notes: No existing RT definitions require modification.
Future regime derivations attach beneath Orientation.
Orientation classifies RT operational regimes without privileging any specific regime family.
The classification remains downstream of RT_core and does not introduce a temporal primitive.
This patch is governance and architecture only.
Orientation organizes and classifies operational regimes, but does not supersede RT_core or privilege any specific regime family.
